I guess I never realized how vast were the services provided by the humble, local health department. Immunizations, Medicaid, Prenatal care, Birth/Death Certificates, Child Care Licensing, among multiple other services.

So if you wonder how the government has access to practically all of our children’s health information, well, here is the connection. They start chasing babies at conception, and don’t let go.

*How many kids can the government access through the health department? *

They provide Medicaid insurance to low income children (and thereby are entitled to their medical records). They provide no/low-cost immunizations to practically all children. They are the repository for every immunization administered in the state. They partner with other agencies to provide insurance to children who don’t qualify for Medicaid (more medical record access).

Clinical & Nutritional Services: Primary Care (for uninsured adults and children), Dental Services (for non/underinsured children, pregnant women and adults), Laboratory Services (County residents and visitors), School Based Health Services, Women’s Health, Men’s Health, Teen Health, Family Planning, Refugee Health; Environmental Health: Child Care Licensing, Water Programs, Storage Tanks, Onsite Sewage Disposal and Septic Tanks, Inspections; Infectious Disease Services: Disease reporting, Epidemiology, HIV/AIDS, STD Testing/Treatment, Hepatitis, TB Control Program; Wellness Programs: Health Promotion, Teen Resources, Kids Health Fun; Emergency Preparedness and Response: Emergency Planning, Surveillance, Response Training; Community Health Planning and Statistics: Data and Reports, Health Information Management, Health Equity
